title: Alice in Wonderland
intro: Strange Company - A Way Out / The Driest Story / Prizes and Dinah / Mary Ann! / Far Too Much Alice / Bill and the Chimney / One Small Cake
ending: Alice is free of the house, with the moonlit forest path ahead.

stageLabel: Alice and her companions in Wonderland

steps.text: Excuse me. Do you know a way out?
The bank is close. Can you swim a little farther?
Yes. I would rather be small on dry land.
Everyone here? Stay clear of the slippery edge.
All of us. Though I am still dripping.
We slipped in too. There must be somewhere dry.
My feathers are quite soaked.
Perhaps we can help one another.
That door must lead somewhere drier.
Then let us get out together.
Somewhere we can sit would be very welcome.
A little company makes this place less strange.

steps.text: Sit close. I know a very dry story.
Long ago, a king claimed a country, and the lords argued over his claim.
My feathers have not noticed.
Perhaps a dry story is not quite the same as dry clothes.
Then we need a Caucus-Race.
What sort of race is that?
Run round here. Begin when you like, and stop when you like.
How shall we know who has won?
I shall decide when we are dry.
That will do. The race is finished.
And who is the winner?
Every one of us. There must be prizes.

steps.text: Four sweets. One for each of you.
But you ran too, Alice.
I have only my thimble left.
Then accept this very fine prize.
Thank you. I shall take good care of it.
I wish Dinah could see us.
Who is Dinah?
My cat at home. She is wonderfully good at catching mice and birds.
A cat is very different company for a mouse.
And for a bird. Come along.
I think we had better go.
I am sorry. I did not mean to frighten you.
I was thinking of my friend. I forgot what she would be to them.

steps.text: My gloves! My fan! Where did I drop them?
You dropped them in the hall, beside the pool.
Mary Ann! Fetch another pair and a fan from my house.
Mary Ann? I think you mean someone else.
My housemaid. The house is along that path.
But my name is Alice.
Please hurry. I cannot go without them.
I am not his housemaid. Still, I can try to help.
W. Rabbit. This must be the house.
How curious to be sent on an errand by a rabbit.
Perhaps I can put one thing right today.
Only the gloves and fan. Then I can find my own way.

steps.text: A fan and clean gloves. At least those are easy to find.
Another bottle, and no label. I wonder what this one will do.
I am tired of being so tiny. Perhaps this will make me grow again.
A little. That is quite enough.
Oh! It is not stopping.
I cannot stand up. The ceiling is too low.
I wanted to grow, not to fill the whole house.
I cannot get out at this size.
Footsteps outside. The Rabbit must be coming back.

scenes.name: Bill and the Chimney
scenes.atmosphere: Moonlit cottage; a surprising rescue attempt.

steps.text: Something enormous is blocking my door!
Bill! Bring your ladder. Try the chimney!
The chimney? All right. I will try.
Someone is coming down the chimney! One little kick should send them back up!
I think I shall stay out here.
That did not work. Toss a few little pebbles down the chimney!
Those pebbles have turned into little cakes!
Perhaps one of them can help me get out.

scenes.name: One Small Cake
scenes.atmosphere: A small bite, a clear path and moonlit freedom.

steps.text: Only a small bite. I have had quite enough of growing.
Smaller. At last!
The room looks enormous again. I am nearly small enough.
I can move again. And this time, I am staying small.
The door. I must get out before the Rabbit sees me.
There she goes!
No more bottles. No more errands. Just the path.
The trees are close. I can find my own way.
